title: Daily Signal Brief 006 — EU AI Act Annex III pushed to Dec 2027; NYC AEDT $15K–$45K/AEDT/month; EC consultation closes June 23
summary: L4 Critical: the AI Digital Omnibus political agreement (May 7 trilogue, now propagating into counsel briefings) postpones EU AI Act Annex III high-risk obligations — including employment AI — from 2026-08-02 to 2027-12-02. The deadline forcing function on buyer procurement just disappeared for 16 months; Mobley v. Workday and NYC AEDT are now the proximate pressures. Stratum's posture should not soften — the Compact's bar was set by the standard, not the deadline. Compass should publish a one-paragraph customer note this week ('the rule is the same; the clock is longer; our readiness is unchanged'); Helm should consider a Briefing paragraph on standard-led posture; Forge should re-baseline the internal compliance roadmap so nothing accelerates and nothing delays. L3 Action: the NY Comptroller's December 2025 audit found NYC DCWP's AEDT enforcement 'ineffective' (75% of 311 calls misrouted; auditors found 17 violations where DCWP found 1), and DCWP has committed to proactive 2026 enforcement. Buyer-side objection 'no one's enforcing it' is now refutable with $15K–$45K per AEDT per month — Compass updates the AEDT page, Vector adds to Cordova and Halcyon next-touch briefs. L2 Watch: the European Commission published draft Annex III guidelines on 2026-05-19, public consultation closes 2026-06-23 — a low-cost, time-boxed opportunity for Stratum to put credible language into the regulatory record. Tier-2 decision for Helm by 2026-06-09 on whether to file; Forge + Kernel co-draft if approved.
